h1: The 5 Best Cordless Shop Vacuums for Garage and Job Site Cleanup, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Shop Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 cordless wet dry shop vacuums for garages and job sites, compared on battery platform, tank size, run time and price.
summary: The DEWALT 20V MAX shop vacuum is the pick for anyone already on that battery platform, with a name that stands behind parts and packs. The CRAFTSMAN 2 gallon is the strongest value if you own V20 batteries, the Seesii is the best self-contained option, and the Vacmaster is the cheapest way to get 2.5 gallons of wet dry capacity.
intro: Cordless shop vacuums come with a hidden tax: the battery. Many of the best-known units are sold tool-only, which means the sticker price is a fraction of what you spend if you do not already own the packs, and the run time you get depends entirely on which pack you slot in. Buyers who miss this end up with a vacuum that does nothing until a second purchase arrives.

This ranking sorts five models by what they actually offer on paper. We reviewed each from its listing and spec sheet, comparing platform, tank size where it is stated, run time where a figure is given, and price bracket. A shop vac is a messy-job tool, so we favored durability signals and battery flexibility over gadget lists. Where a listing leaves out suction ratings or tank size, we flag it.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Shop Vacuum Wet and Dry
products.verdict: A wet and dry vac on the DEWALT 20V MAX platform, with the broadest battery ecosystem here.
products.description:
The DEWALT is a cordless wet and dry shop vacuum designed around the 20V MAX battery system, priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. It handles both liquid spills and dry debris, which is the baseline for a proper shop vac.

It ranks first because the platform matters more than any feature on a spec sheet. DEWALT's 20V MAX batteries are among the most widely owned in the trade, so if you have a drill or saw on that platform, the vacuum comes with a ready-made power supply and replacement packs are easy to find. Against the CRAFTSMAN below, the main edge is ecosystem depth and a strong service network rather than raw capacity.

Buy it if you already own DEWALT packs and want a vacuum that matches. The caveat is that the listing does not give tank size or suction ratings, and a battery is often sold separately, so confirm the box contents.
pros: Replacement packs are easy to find
cons: Tank size not stated in listing
products.idealFor: Anyone already invested in DEWALT 20V MAX tools.
products.skipIf: You have no 20V batteries and want an all-in-one kit.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMCV002B 20V Max 2 gallon Wet Dry Vac (Tool Only)
products.verdict: A 2 gallon wet dry vac for V20 owners, sold without a battery or charger.
products.description:
The CMCV002B is a 2 gallon cordless wet dry vacuum from CRAFTSMAN, sold as tool only, so it ships without a battery or charger. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It takes second place because the 2 gallon tank is a practical size for garage and car cleanup: large enough to swallow a day of sawdust, small enough to carry in one hand. Compared with the DEWALT, the listing is more transparent, giving a clear capacity. The tradeoff is that you are paying vacuum money for a body that needs batteries you may have to buy, so the real cost is higher for newcomers.

It makes sense if you already run CRAFTSMAN 20V Max batteries. If not, check the total price with a pack before treating it as a bargain.
cons: Small tank fills fast on big jobs
products.idealFor: CRAFTSMAN battery owners cleaning garages and vehicles.
products.skipIf: You start with no 20V batteries at all.

products.name: Seesii Cordless Wet Dry Shop Vac
products.verdict: A cordless wet dry vac with a listed 20 minute run time, aimed at buyers without a tool brand.
products.description:
The Seesii is a cordless wet dry shop vacuum with a listed run time of 20 minutes, priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. Its appeal is that it appears to be a complete unit rather than a bare tool.

It ranks third because a stated run time is more useful than a vague promise. Twenty minutes is typical for this class and enough for a garage floor or a car interior in one pass, though not for continuous work on a job site. It sits below the DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN on brand support and battery interchangeability, since a stand-alone pack cannot be borrowed from your drill.

It suits renters and homeowners who do not own any cordless tools. The honest caveat is that it lists no tank capacity or filter details.
products.idealFor: Homeowners with no existing 20V tool batteries.
products.skipIf: You want to share batteries with other tools.

products.name: TaskStar Cordless Shop Vac
products.verdict: A near twin of the Seesii on paper, with the same 20 minute run time and price band.
products.description:
The TaskStar is another cordless shop vac with a listed 20 minute run time, in the $100 to $200 bracket. On the spec sheet it matches the Seesii almost line for line.

It ranks fourth only because there is less to separate it and because a newer brand name offers little track record on spare parts or support. With identical run time and price, the choice often comes down to which listing gives clearer accessories, hose length and warranty terms, and neither gives much.

It is worth a look if the Seesii is out of stock or priced higher. Beyond that, it is a cross-check rather than a first choice.
pros: Same price band as the Seesii
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a standalone unit and a second quote.
products.skipIf: You value brand support and spare parts.

products.name: Vacmaster DVOM202P 1101 2.5-Gal 20V Cordless Portable Wet/Dry Vac Red
products.verdict: The largest tank here at 2.5 gallons and the lowest price bracket of the group.
products.description:
The Vacmaster DVOM202P is a 20V cordless portable wet and dry vacuum with a 2.5 gallon tank, priced in the $50 to $100 bracket. It is both the biggest and the cheapest unit in this ranking.

It ranks last because cost savings come with open questions. The listing does not state run time, nor does it confirm whether a battery ships with the tool, and a vacuum with a bigger tank than its rivals still needs sustained suction to be useful. Against the CRAFTSMAN, you gain a half gallon and lose some brand weight.

It is a smart pick for occasional garage cleanup when the budget is tight. For daily use, spend toward the DEWALT.
products.idealFor: Occasional garage and car cleanup on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You use a shop vac daily on job sites.

whatMatters.factor: Battery platform and what ships in the box
whatMatters.detail: A tool-only vacuum has no battery or charger, so the real price is the body plus a pack. If you own 20V MAX or V20 tools already, you may be able to share packs. Read the title for the words tool only before comparing prices.

Cordless shop vacs run from about 1 to 2.5 gallons, much smaller than a corded 5 to 16 gallon unit. A 2 gallon tank handles workshop sweeping and car interiors but fills quickly on a drywall job. Check the gallon figure on the listing, since several skip it.

A 20 minute run time sounds fine, but it is measured at a given power mode, usually the lowest. At full suction, expect much less. A bigger battery in amp-hours extends the time, so check the pack size, not only the minutes.

Wet and dry vacs use a foam sleeve or a cartridge filter, and you must change filters between wet and dry use. Fine dust, such as from drywall or a sander, clogs paper filters fast. Look for washable cartridges and read the manual note on which filter to use for which job.

A short hose or a stiff one makes a cordless vac awkward on stairs and in cars. Accessories like a crevice tool and a floor nozzle matter more than a long list of extras. Check hose length and see whether the unit has on-board storage for the tools.

howToChoose.subheading: For Car and Garage Cleanup Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact tank around 2 gallons, wet pickup for spills, and a hose that reaches the back seat. Weight matters more than capacity for this job.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN 2 gallon for balance, the Seesii for a no-battery-needed unit, and the Vacmaster if you want the most room for the least money.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You work on job sites, share batteries across tools or expect to keep the vacuum for years. The DEWALT 20V MAX is the most sensible long-term purchase.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean a garage or car a few times a year. The Vacmaster covers it at the lowest price bracket.

faq.q: Will a 20V battery from another tool fit these?
faq.a: Only if the platform matches. The DEWALT uses 20V MAX packs and the CRAFTSMAN uses its own 20V Max system, so cross-brand packs usually do not fit. Check the battery interface in the manual before assuming compatibility.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Overlooking tool only. The listed price is just the vacuum body, and a battery plus charger can add as much again if you start from zero.

faq.q: Is a cordless shop vac worth it over a corded one?
faq.a: For cars, workbenches and quick spills, yes, since there is no cord to drag. For big jobs and fine dust, a corded model has far more suction and a bigger tank, so keep one if you do renovation work.

faq.q: How do I use one for wet pickup?
faq.a: Remove any paper filter, fit the foam sleeve if your model uses one, and empty the tank before it reaches the float. Let the filter dry before using the vacuum for dust again.

faq.q: How should I maintain the filter?
faq.a: Tap out dry dust after each session and rinse washable cartridges when they look clogged. A blocked filter cuts suction and shortens run time, so replace it if cleaning no longer helps.

faq.q: Can a cordless unit handle drywall dust?
faq.a: Fine dust clogs filters quickly and can damage the motor if the filter is wrong. Use a fine-dust or HEPA-rated filter if available, and expect to empty and clean the unit often.

finalTake: The DEWALT 20V MAX is the pick for anyone on that battery platform, and the CRAFTSMAN 2 gallon is the better fit if your batteries are CRAFTSMAN. The Seesii is the most sensible standalone for people with no cordless tools, while the Vacmaster is the budget option with the largest tank. Check whether a battery is included before you compare prices.
